scenarios.name: empty_query
scenarios.description: An empty DiscoveryQuery (no predicates specified) must match all instances in the repository.

scenarios.name: tier_filter_note
scenarios.description: A tier:0 filter returns only Note instances (Tier 0). Tier 2 instances must not appear.

scenarios.name: tier_filter_record
scenarios.description: A tier:2 filter returns only Record instances (Tier 2). Tier 0 instances must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_name_article
scenarios.description: A typeName:'article' filter returns exactly all Records whose typeNamespace-qualified type name is 'article'. Tier 0 instances and Records of other types must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_namespace
scenarios.description: A typeNamespace:'com.example.discovery' filter returns all Tier 2 Records in that namespace. Tier 0 instances have no typeNamespace and must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_id_project
scenarios.description: A typeId filter matching the 'project' type UUID returns exactly the two project Records.

scenarios.name: container_alpha
scenarios.description: A containerId filter for container-alpha returns only the three articles registered as members via memberInstanceIds. Instances not in that container must not appear.

scenarios.name: container_beta
scenarios.description: A containerId filter for container-beta returns only the two project Records registered as members via memberInstanceIds.

scenarios.name: single_tag_searchable
scenarios.description: A tag filter for ['searchable'] returns all instances carrying that tag string. Instances without the tag must not appear.

scenarios.name: multi_tag_and
scenarios.description: A tag filter for ['searchable', 'indexed'] uses AND semantics: only instances carrying BOTH tags must be returned. Instances carrying only one of the two tags must not appear.

scenarios.name: lifecycle_published
scenarios.description: A lifecycleState:'published' filter returns only Records in that lifecycle state. Records in other states and Tier 0 instances (which have no lifecycleState) must not appear.

scenarios.name: lifecycle_draft
scenarios.description: A lifecycleState:'draft' filter returns only Records in the draft state.

scenarios.name: type_and_lifecycle_combined
scenarios.description: Combined typeName and lifecycleState predicates are evaluated as an AND conjunction. Only Records satisfying both must be returned.

scenarios.name: content_match_discovery
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'discovery' predicate must include every instance whose Text Projection contains a segment whose normalized text contains 'discovery' as a substring. The guaranteed-recall floor is articles 1, 2, and 4 (title/body contain 'discovery') and project-2 (description contains 'discovery'). Implementations may return additional instances.

scenarios.name: content_match_indexing
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'indexing' predicate must include every instance with a Text Projection segment containing 'indexing'. Articles 1 and 3 each have 'indexing' as a multiselect topics value. This tests that multiselect elements each contribute a separate segment.

scenarios.name: content_match_indexed_tag_and_label
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'indexed' predicate must include instances where 'indexed' appears in tag segments (articles 1, 3 and project-1) and in the string label field of metric-1 ('Indexed Record Count'). This tests that both tag segments and string field segments are projected.

scenarios.name: content_match_combined_type_and_content
scenarios.description: Combined typeName and contentMatch predicates: must return only article instances (structured filter, exact) that also match the content floor for 'draft' (the select field value 'draft' is searchable). The floor is articles 2 and 5 (both have status field value 'draft').

scenarios.name: i120_include_format_markdown
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype string with format markdown is searchable. Recall floor — the article carrying it must be found.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_first
scenarios.description: I-120: a list-cardinality string emits one segment per array element. Element 0 must be independently recallable.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_middle
scenarios.description: I-120: element 1 of the same open list. Asserted separately from element 0 so a projection that concatenates the list into a single segment still passes only if every element is recallable.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_last
scenarios.description: I-120: element 2 of the same open list. See the README note on what this trio does NOT assert (segment count and order are not observable through DiscoveryHit).

scenarios.name: i120_list_segments_order
scenarios.description: srs#483/#317-F2: expectedSegments asserts segment COUNT and ORDER directly, closing the gap the i120_include_list_element_* trio leaves open (each of those only proves independent recallability). Same field as that trio: article-1's open list-cardinality 'aliases', which I-120 requires to emit one segment per array element in array order.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_format_uuid
scenarios.description: I-120: format uuid contributes no segment. The token is the uuid's own leading group and appears nowhere else in the fixture, so any hit means the excluded Field was projected. Asserted against the allow-list (CC-25), not as a format!=uri test.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_format_email
scenarios.description: I-120: format email contributes no segment. Same allow-list reasoning as the uuid case.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_integer
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype integer contributes no segment. Distinct from the legacy `number` exclusion — the erratum added integer as its own datatype.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_date_time
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype date-time contributes no segment. Distinct from `date`; the erratum made date-time a first-class datatype rather than a string format.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_map_value
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype map contributes no segment. The probe is a map VALUE, the likelier of the two to be projected by an implementation that walks the carrier generically.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_map_key
scenarios.description: I-120: a map's KEYS are not segments either. Asserted separately from the value: a projection that emitted keys but not values would pass the value case alone.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_ref_reference
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype ref in mode reference contributes no segment. The probe is the referenced project's own instance id — a hit would mean opaque identifiers are searchable as prose. project-1 is NOT expected: a content match is over Text Projection segments, and no segment contains this id.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_ref_inline
scenarios.description: I-120 + CC-27: datatype ref in mode inline contributes no segment either, knowingly. The token sits in the nested composite's `display_name`, a plain string Field that WOULD be searchable at the top level. Recursive composite Text Projection is undefined — this fixture asserts exclusion only, and the unfindability is a recorded accepted cost.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_dependent
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype dependent contributes no segment. Excluded by its own datatype — the projection does not resolve `dependsOn` (here, the searchable `title`) before deciding.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_number
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype number contributes no segment. Probes `legacy_score`, whose value appears in no projectable string anywhere in the fixture — `word_count`'s values (42, 28, 150, 75, 99) are all too short to probe meaningfully.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_boolean
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype boolean contributes no segment. No projectable string in the fixture contains "true" or "false", so a hit means a boolean was rendered into a segment — `is_published` is true on two articles and `is_active` on one metric. Assumes the rendering would be the JSON literal, which is the only plausible one; a projection emitting "1"/"yes" would evade this and no assertion can cover every rendering of a value with no text.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_date
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype date contributes no segment. "2025-01-01" occurs exactly once in the fixture — as article-4's `publish_date`, the excluded Field itself — so any hit means the date was projected. Distinct from `date-time` (i120_exclude_date_time), which the Rev-7 erratum made a separate datatype.
